requirements.requirement: Process every job listed in spool/jobs.tsv exactly once into /srv/legacy2/print-spool-recovery/printed, preserving payload bytes and retaining the original spool files.
requirements.summary: The manifest lists J100 and J101. Each was recovered to one corresponding archive file; source and destination SHA-256 hashes match, the two source files remain, and the same state persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provide a working CUPS queue named archive that writes completed jobs electronically to the printed directory without requiring a physical printer.
requirements.summary: The archive queue uses the custom archive directory URI, accepts jobs, remains enabled and idle, and CUPS is enabled and active. The queue and service recovered after a verified node restart.

requirements.requirement: Archive each newly submitted raw job to the same printed directory as one byte-preserving file.
requirements.summary: Two live raw submissions completed as cups-1.prn and cups-2.prn. Direct comparisons and matching hashes prove byte preservation, including a submission made after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged across execution and restart. CUPS 2.4.10-18.el10 was installed from the platform repositories and demonstrated working behavior.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Both staged jobs were archived exactly once with matching bytes and retained originals; the archive CUPS queue successfully processed raw jobs before and after reboot; and the operating-system release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged reboot with observed disconnect, a different post-restart boot ID, recovered service and data, and a successful post-restart job. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Exact-once verification is based on the observed expected archive filenames, bounded instance counts, and directory listings rather than a content-wide duplicate search under arbitrary unrelated names.
The lifecycle collector independently confirms the reboot identity and platform but does not independently probe CUPS or archived data; those recovery observations come from executor commands.

The package-install output is truncated, so the precise dependency responsible for the new Avahi listener is not fully visible, although the listener was absent after preparation and present after execution.
Requirement staged-job-recovery cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles: installing CUPS and SELinux tooling, creating and labeling the archive directory and backend, recovering the staged jobs, configuring the queue, submitting bounded probes, and rebooting. No failed services or package damage remained. Minor retained residue consists of two evidence input files in /tmp, created by cmd-2c1d1be0780240bb and cmd-ef7f078f41044519 and not removed. The CUPS installation also left Avahi listening on UDP 5353 on all interfaces; that discovery exposure was not shown necessary for this local electronic archive and remained after execution. No reverted, unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified.
